title: A non-invasive method to genotype cephalopod sex by quantitative PCR

To identify autosomal and sex-linked primers in I. illecebrosus, a set of primers was first designed for D. pealeii using orthologous genes identified by GENESPACE targeting chromosome Dpe01 (“autosome” primer) and chromosome Dpe43 (“sex” primer). Next, short-read sequencing data was generated from 20 I. illecebrosus individuals (10 males and 10 females, as determined by gonad morphology). Specifically, squid DNA was extracted using a DNeasy Blood & Tissue Kit (Qiagen) following the manufacturer’s instructions, and DNA extracts were purified and cleaned from short DNA fragments using TotalPure NGS Mag-Bind Beads (Omega Bio-tek). Low-coverage Whole Genome Sequencing Illumina libraries were prepared using the miniaturized Nextera DNA Library Preparation Kit with an Echo liquid handler and sequenced by the Genomics and Cell Characterization Core Facility (GC3F) at the University of Oregon using an Illumina NovaSeq 6000. Raw sequencing data was processed using grenepipe71 by aligning to the D. pealeii reference genome (GCA_023376005.1). The resulting BAM files were used to make a consensus using the SAMtools consensus tool.72

Frozen arm tips from O. bimaculoides, S. officinalis, E. berryi, and D. pealeii were obtained as flash frozen samples, while I. illecebrosus and I. argentinus samples were obtained as mantle fragments or arm tips preserved in 95% ethanol. All samples were temporarily stored at −80°C until DNA extraction. To extract genomic DNA, ∼3 mm pieces of tissue were placed in 1.5 mL Safe-Lock tubes and processed using the Monarch Spin gDNA Extraction Kit. Briefly, 200 μL of Tissue Lysis Buffer and 10 μL of 20 mg/mL Proteinase K were added to each tube, and the samples were incubated at 56°C in a ThermoMixer shaking at 1400 rpm for 1–2 h until fully digested. In some cases, the lysate turned pink or purple, due to chromatophore pigments. Following digestion, 400 μL of Binding Buffer was added, samples were pulse vortexed for 5–10 s, and the lysates were transferred to gDNA Purification Columns. Columns were centrifuged at 1,000 x g for 3 min followed by > 12,000 x g for 1 min, washed twice with 500 μL of gDNA Wash Buffer, and eluted with 60 μL of pre-warmed (60°C) gDNA Elution Buffer after a 5-min incubation at room temperature. Eluted DNA concentrations ranged from ∼50 to 350 ng/μL. All DNA was diluted 20-fold (no further normalization required) and transferred into 8-well strips for subsequent qPCR.

DNA extractions were performed using a Monarch Spin gDNA Extraction Kit with minor modifications to the manufacturer’s protocol, described below. Juvenile A. bandense were carefully caught with a soft net and positioned dorsal side up without anesthesia. A sterile foam swab was pre-soaked in tank water and gently stroked across the dorsal mantle skin from anterior to posterior, avoiding the anterior tip of the mantle (the most delicate region of the skin). As a practical note, swabbing adult A. bandense requires substantially greater pressure than juvenile animals, likely due to the presence of mucus on the skin. The animal was gently rotated ventral side up, and the other side of the swab was used to swab the ventral surface with slightly greater pressure. Each animal was placed in an individual tank to keep track of its identity, and the swab was placed face down into a 1.5 mL Safe-Lock tube preloaded with 200 μL Tissue Lysis Buffer and 3 μL of 20 mg/mL Proteinase K. After all samples were collected, swab shafts were trimmed to allow tube closure, and samples were incubated at 56°C in a ThermoMixer shaking at 1400 rpm for 1 h. The shortened shaft of each swab was then held tightly while the swab was pressed and dragged against the side of the tube to recover liquid from the foam tip. Next, 400 μL of Binding Buffer was added, the samples were pulse vortexed for 5–10 s, and the lysate was transferred to gDNA Purification Columns. Columns were centrifuged at 1,000 x g for 3 min followed by > 12,000 x g for 1 min, washed twice with 500 μL of gDNA Wash Buffer, and eluted after a 5-min incubation with 200 μL of pre-warmed (60°C) gDNA Elution Buffer. The DNA yield from an animal of 10–20 mm mantle length was typically ∼250 ng, although yields varied widely across samples. DNA was transferred into 8-well strips for qPCR, with no further normalization of concentration required.

qPCR reactions were performed on a QuantStudio 5 Real-Time PCR System (Applied Biosystems) using 2X SYBR Green qPCR Master Mix (APExBIO) with ROX reference dye (APExBIO). Reactions were prepared as technical repeats in quadruplicate (7 μL total volume, 0.25 μM forward primer, 0.25 μM reverse primer, 2 μL template DNA). Thermocycling conditions were as follows: initial denaturation (95°C for 2 min), amplification (95°C for 15 s, 60°C for 45 s, for a total of 45 cycles), melt curve analysis (95°C for 15 s, 60°C for 1 min, followed by an increase to 95°C at a rate of 0.06 °C/s).

steps.title: Maintain cuttlefish housing conditions
steps.instruction: House dwarf cuttlefish (Ascarosepion bandense) in a recirculating system with 30–35 ppt artificial seawater (Rea Sea Coral Pro Salt) at 24 °C–25 °C; keep ammonia at 0 ppm, nitrite <0.1 ppm, nitrate <20 ppm, pH 8.0–8.4; feed live mysid shrimp to animals <40 days post‑hatch, then live grass shrimp, three times daily.

steps.title: Handle cuttlefish per IACUC protocol
steps.instruction: Handle all cuttlefish according to approved IACUC protocol AC‑AABT8673, using deep anesthesia and minimizing suffering as described in the institutional guidelines.

steps.title: Obtain frozen tissue samples
steps.instruction: Collect frozen arm tips from Octopus bimaculoides, Sepia officinalis, Euprymna berryi, and Doryteuthis pealeii (MBL necropsy) and mantle tissue or arm tips preserved in 95 % ethanol from Illex illecebrosus (collected 1–2 Aug 2024 off US east coast, lat 38.515, ‑73.309) and Illex argentinus (collected 5 Mar 2024 off Falkland Islands, lat ‑49.237, ‑60.837).

steps.title: Store samples at –80 °C
steps.instruction: Temporarily store all frozen arm tips, mantle fragments, and ethanol‑preserved samples at –80 °C until DNA extraction.

steps.title: Extract genomic DNA from frozen tissue
steps.instruction: Cut ~3 mm pieces of frozen tissue, place each in a 1.5 mL Safe‑Lock tube, add 200 µL Tissue Lysis Buffer and 10 µL of 20 mg/mL Proteinase K, incubate at 56 °C in a ThermoMixer shaking at 1400 rpm for 1–2 h (until fully digested; lysate may turn pink/purple). Add 400 µL Binding Buffer, pulse‑vortex 5–10 s, transfer lysate to Monarch Spin gDNA Purification Column, centrifuge 1,000 × g 3 min then >12,000 × g 1 min, wash twice with 500 µL Wash Buffer, elute with 60 µL pre‑warmed (60 °C) Elution Buffer after 5‑min RT incubation. DNA concentration will be ~50–350 ng/µL; dilute 20‑fold (no further normalization) and transfer to 8‑well strip for qPCR.

steps.title: Extract gDNA from adult/juvenile A. bandense swabs
steps.instruction: For each juvenile, place a sterile foam swab (pre‑soaked in tank water) face‑down in a 1.5 mL Safe‑Lock tube containing 200 µL Tissue Lysis Buffer and 3 µL 20 mg/mL Proteinase K. After collection, trim swab shaft, incubate at 56 °C, 1400 rpm for 1 h. Press swab against tube wall to recover liquid, add 400 µL Binding Buffer, pulse‑vortex 5–10 s, transfer to purification column, centrifuge as above, wash twice with 500 µL Wash Buffer, elute with 200 µL pre‑warmed (60 °C) Elution Buffer after 5‑min RT incubation. Typical yield ≈250 ng per 10–20 mm mantle length animal. Transfer eluate to 8‑well strip (no further normalization).

steps.title: Swab 3‑hour‑old hatchlings and extract DNA
steps.instruction: Fill a 5 L jug with seawater, cover with a soft microfiber towel so the towel surface sits ~5 mm below water. Catch 3‑hour‑old hatchlings with a turkey baster, place on towel, lift towel edges to expose mantle above water, swab dorsal mantle with a sterile foam swab (pre‑soaked in tank water) using extremely low pressure, rotate hatchling ventral‑up and swab ventral mantle. Place each swab in a 1.5 mL Safe‑Lock tube with 200 µL Tissue Lysis Buffer and 3 µL Proteinase K, trim shaft, incubate 56 °C, 1400 rpm for 1 h, recover liquid, add 400 µL Binding Buffer, vortex 5–10 s, purify as above, elute in 50 µL pre‑warmed (60 °C) Elution Buffer. Typical yield ≈13 ng. Transfer to 8‑well strip (no normalization). After qPCR, keep hatchlings in individual tanks, group by predicted sex for 2 weeks, then euthanize in 10 % ethanol in artificial seawater, take a small tissue piece and process with the frozen‑tissue DNA extraction protocol.

steps.title: Design primers using Geneious
steps.instruction: For A. bandense, O. bimaculoides, S. officinalis, E. berryi, D. pealeii, open Geneious Prime 2025.2.2, use modified Primer3 (v2.3.7) with parameters: optimal primer size 20 bp, optimal Tm 59 °C, GC % 50 %, product size 100–200 bp, GC clamp = 1, max poly‑X = 3, max dimer Tm = 30 °C. Screen primers by BLAST against the appropriate reference genome and evaluate secondary structure/self‑complementarity with IDT OligoAnalyzer.

steps.title: Generate primer pairs with ceph pipeline
steps.instruction: For I. argentinus and I. illecebrosus, run the script ceph_primer_pipeline.sh (github.com/stsmall/ceph_primer_pipeline). Provide a GFF file and reference genome FASTA; the script extracts user‑selected features with BEDTools, builds FASTA entries for Primer3, and uses Primer3 (optimal size 20 bp, Tm 60 °C, GC % 50 %, product 150–300 bp, max poly‑X = 5) to design primers. MFEprimer checks specificity. Modify Primer3 config to return a single primer set per entry; export final primer sets as a CSV file.

steps.title: Validate primers by PCR and sequencing
steps.instruction: Test each primer pair on genomic DNA from confirmed male and female individuals (using the frozen‑tissue or swab DNA extracts) and on no‑template controls. Run qPCR (see step 11) in quadruplicate; select primer pairs that produce a single, template‑dependent melt curve. Verify amplicon size on 2 % agarose gel, then submit PCR product for Oxford Nanopore sequencing (Plasmidsaurus, Premium PCR Sequencing). Confirm sequence matches reference. Determine primer efficiency by a dilution series; accept efficiencies between 90 %–110 % in the assay concentration range. Choose one autosomal and one sex‑linked primer pair per species for downstream sex genotyping.

steps.title: Prepare qPCR reactions
steps.instruction: In a clean PCR hood, assemble 7 µL reactions using 2X SYBR Green qPCR Master Mix (APExBIO) with ROX reference dye: 0.25 µM forward primer, 0.25 µM reverse primer, 2 µL template DNA (diluted 20‑fold), and nuclease‑free water to volume. Prepare each reaction in quadruplicate technical repeats.

steps.title: Run qPCR on QuantStudio 5
steps.instruction: Load reactions onto a QuantStudio 5 Real‑Time PCR System (Applied Biosystems) using a 384‑well Optical Plate. Run the following program: 95 °C 2 min initial denaturation; 45 cycles of 95 °C 15 s, 60 °C 45 s; melt curve 95 °C 15 s, 60 °C 1 min, then increase to 95 °C at 0.06 °C/s. Use QuantStudio Design & Analysis Software v2.2.0 for automatic Cq, mean, and SEM calculation.

steps.title: Analyze qPCR data and assign sex
steps.instruction: Discard outlier replicates with Cq deviating >1 cycle from the mean. Compute ΔCq = Cq(autosome) − Cq(sex chromosome) for each sample; clusters will form two groups. Calculate ΔΔCq = ΔCq − median(ΔCq of male cluster) (or male standard). Use a threshold of –0.5 (midpoint ΔΔCq) to call male (ΔΔCq > ‑0.5) or female (ΔΔCq < ‑0.5). If the mean ΔΔCq lies within 1 SEM of the threshold, repeat the assay. Record SEM as the sum of SEMs from autosome and sex replicate groups.

steps.title: Perform statistical analyses in MATLAB
steps.instruction: Import ΔΔCq values into MATLAB R2024b. For each species, test whether the observed correct‑prediction rate exceeds 50 % using a one‑sided exact binomial test. Compare male vs. female ΔΔCq means with unpaired two‑sample Student’s t‑test (use one‑sample t‑test against zero for O. bimaculoides, which has only one male). Consider p < 0.05 significant. Plot results as box‑and‑whisker graphs (median, IQR, whiskers to ±1.5 × IQR).

steps.title: Prepare data for synteny analysis
steps.instruction: Download peptide and GTF files for D. pealeii and E. scolopes from their publications; obtain the unpublished E. berryi assembly (cell atlas). Use the existing S. esculenta annotation (liftover from S. pharaonis). Since no S. officinalis annotation existed, generate one by lifting over the S. pharaonis annotation with Liftoff (default settings).

steps.title: Run synteny analyses
steps.instruction: Perform synteny mapping between chromosomes of S. esculenta, S. officinalis, E. berryi, E. scolopes, D. pealeii, and O. bimaculoides using GENESPACE v1.2.3 (R package) with E. scolopes as reference; set useOrder = False to scale chromosomes by physical position. For A. bandense (non‑chromosome‑level assembly), align to E. scolopes with minimap2 (‑cx asm20) to locate putative Z contigs.

steps.title: Identify autosomal and sex‑linked primers in I. illecebrosus
steps.instruction: Design primers for D. pealeii targeting chromosome Dpe01 (autosome) and Dpe43 (sex) using orthologous genes identified by GENESPACE. Generate short‑read Illumina data for 20 I. illecebrosus individuals (10 M, 10 F) by extracting DNA with the DNeasy Blood & Tissue Kit (Qiagen), cleaning with TotalPure NGS Mag‑Bind Beads (Omega Bio‑tek), preparing low‑coverage WGS libraries with the miniaturized Nextera kit (Echo liquid handler), and sequencing on an Illumina NovaSeq 6000 (GC3F, Univ. of Oregon). Process raw reads with grenepipe, align to D. pealeii reference (GCA_023376005.1), and create consensus sequences using SAMtools consensus.
